messages.author: 9e8158251f947302
messages.subject: debug= option in rhwatch() in 0.73
parts:
I'm unsure how to reproduce under v0.73 some desirable error handling behavior from earlier versions.

I'm submitting an R script via R CMD BATCH which contains multiple Rhipe jobs in a for loop.  Previously, if some R code within my map expression produced an error on the node, Rhipe would write the error to output (along with some Java errors usually), kill the job and produce an R error in the script which submitted the Rhipe job.  This was desirable, since it ended my local R session, prevented the for loop in my script from submitting more Rhipe jobs with the same bad code.

It appears that under v0.73 using the default debug=NULL setting, an R error on the node will kill the current Rhipe job, but will not return an R error to the script that created the job.  How can I ask it to produce such an error?

Thanks,
Philip

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] debug= option in rhwatch() in 0.73
parts:
Do you want a variable that contains errors or just produce output? If former,

z=rhwatch(,..debug=NULL, read=FALSE)
and then z[[1]]$rerrors will be TRUE, z[[1]]$errors should contain some info and z[[1]]$state is overall job state (which might not always be correct, since sometimes if the if the job if quick to fail, the R error is not conveyed tto java, trust z[1]]$rerrors. z[[1]]$state is KILLED/FAILED is true, but z[[1]]$state is SUCCESS could be a false positive, hence in the latter case confirm with z[[1]]$rerrors and z[[1]]$errors)

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: debug= option in rhwatch() in 0.73
parts:
Good news tryCatch works.  User operator error.


map=expression({tryCatch({eval(ABSDF)}, error = function(e){ print("Did error"); stop("Did error")})})
eval(map)
x = rhwatch(map=map,input=c(10,1))
